original_question: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. For a feasible n, meaning a positive even integer n >= 20 with n != 22, let T_n be the unique dual graph of such a fullerene. If A is the adjacency matrix of T_n and D is its degree matrix, define the (alpha, beta)-character by ch_{alpha,beta}(T_n) := tr(exp(alpha A + beta D)). For alpha and beta in (0, 1), does equality of this character exactly characterize graph isomorphism among dual fullerenes, meaning that for all feasible n_1, n_2 and dual fullerenes T_{n_1}, T_{n_2}, one has T_{n_1} ≃ T_{n_2} if and only if ch_{alpha,beta}(T_{n_1}) = ch_{alpha,beta}(T_{n_2})?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3 in Section 5.1, restated immediately as Open Problem 4: the uniqueness of the (α, β)-character for dual fullerenes. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right part of the paper: it concerns dual fullerene graphs, uses the same invariant ch_{α,β}(T_n) = tr(exp(αA + βD)), restricts the conjectural uniqueness claim to α, β ∈ (0, 1), and asks whether equality of this invariant is equivalent to graph isomorphism across feasible sizes n_1, n_2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
missing_details: The main inaccuracy is that T_n is not a single uniquely determined graph for each feasible n. The paper uses T_n to denote an arbitrary dual fullerene graph; uniqueness refers to the fact that each fullerene has a unique dual graph, not that there is only one dual fullerene for a given n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
The notation ≃ should be defined explicitly as equality up to graph isomorphism. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
To make the question fully stand-alone, the matrix exponential should be defined as exp(M) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ M^k/k! for every complex-valued square matrix M. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
Definition 5 allows α, β ∈ R in the definition of ch_{α,β}; the restriction α, β ∈ (0, 1) belongs specifically to Conjecture 3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))

If matrix size is to be made explicit, the relevant matrices are those of the dual graph T_n, which has m = n/2 + 2 vertices, so A and D are m × m. This is implicit in the nearby eigenvalue reformulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
The official paper-level formulation is not merely an informal question but the specific task in Open Problem 4: prove or falsify Conjecture 3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))

There are no extra hypotheses here about homogeneity, polynomial degree, or nilpotency; those are inapplicable to this graph-spectral problem and should not be added. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
refined_question: For feasible integers n_1, n_2 (that is, positive even integers n_i ≥ 20 with n_i ≠ 22), let T_{n_1} and T_{n_2} be dual fullerene graphs, and let A_i and D_i denote the adjacency and degree matrices of T_{n_i}. Define, for real α, β, ch_{α,β}(T_{n_i}) := tr(exp(αA_i + βD_i)), where exp(M) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ M^k/k! for square matrices M, and write ≃ for graph isomorphism. Is it true that for every α, β ∈ (0, 1), one has T_{n_1} ≃ T_{n_2} if and only if ch_{α,β}(T_{n_1}) = ch_{α,β}(T_{n_2})? Equivalently, is the (α, β)-character a complete isomorphism invariant for dual fullerene graphs across all feasible sizes? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
justification: The draft clearly targets the character-based uniqueness problem in Section 5.1 rather than the Stone–Wales or cut-partition questions from Section 4. Definition 5 introduces exactly the invariant in your draft, Conjecture 3 states exactly the bidirectional equivalence between isomorphism and equality of character for α, β ∈ (0, 1), and Open Problem 4 asks to prove or falsify that conjecture. The refinement therefore keeps the scope exactly at the paper’s formulation while correcting the mistaken implication that there is a single dual fullerene T_n for each feasible n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.19322))
